end.summary:
- Practised that families can differ in size and in who is part of them; this still needs checking with more examples.
- Practised why sharing household work matters and that children and adults can help; this still needs checking.
- Trisha named family members helping with food, medicine, water, and putting away toys.
- The idea that only grown-ups can help came up again; it was not corrected by the last turn.
end.parentNote: Asha practised family roles and shared household work with Trisha using examples such as bringing medicine, giving water, and putting toys away. Trisha identified several ways family members care for one another, and later recognised that putting away a toy is also help. The mix-up that only grown-ups can do household work remained, so at home you could invite Trisha to name one small task each family member—including them—can do and explain how it helps.
